translations.text: Paul, Silvanus, and Timothy write to the church of the Thessalonians in God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
Grace and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
We ought to thank God for you at all times, brothers and sisters, as is fitting, because your faith is growing abundantly, and the love of each one of you for one another is increasing.
So we ourselves boast about you among the churches of God because of your endurance and faith through all the persecutions and hardships you bear.
This is a sign of God's just judgment, so that you may be worthy of the kingdom of God, for which you are suffering.
Since it is just in God's sight to repay those who afflict you with affliction,
and to give you who are afflicted relief along with us, when our Lord Jesus is revealed from heaven with the angels of his power,
in a flame of fire, he will take vengeance on those who do not know God and those who do not obey the good news of our Lord Jesus.
They will receive a sentence of eternal destruction in the presence of the Lord and the glory of his power,
when he comes to be glorified among his holy people and to be marveled at among all who believe, because his testimony concerning you was believed, on that day.
And we always pray for you for this purpose: that our God may make you worthy of the calling and, by his power, bring you to completion in every good desire and in the work of faith.
So that the name of our Lord Jesus may be glorified in you, and you in him, according to the grace of our God and the Lord Jesus Christ.
We ask you, brothers and sisters, concerning the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ and our gathering to him,
not to be quickly shaken in your minds or alarmed, whether by a spirit, a spoken message, or a letter supposedly from us, claiming that the day of the Lord has drawn near.
So do not let anyone deceive you in any way, for unless the rebellion comes first and the man of lawlessness is revealed, the son of destruction,
the opponent who exalts himself above everyone called a god or worshiped, so that he enters the temple of God and sits down, presenting himself as a god.
Do you not remember that while I was still with you, I used to tell you these things?
Now, then, you know what restrains him, so that he may be revealed at his own time.
For the mystery of lawlessness is already at work; only the one who now restrains it remains until he is out of the way.
Then the lawless one will be revealed, whom the Lord Jesus will destroy with the breath of his mouth and put an end to by the manifestation of his coming.
His coming is through the working of Satan, with every kind of power, signs, and false wonders,
and with every kind of wicked deception for those who will perish, because they did not accept the love of the truth so that they might be saved.
For this reason God will send them a working of deception, so that they believe the lie,
so that everyone who did not believe the truth but set their hearts on wrongdoing will be judged.

But we ought to thank God for you at all times, brothers and sisters loved by the Lord, because God chose you from the beginning for salvation through the Spirit's sanctification and faith in the truth.
He called you to this through our good news, to the salvation of the glory of our Lord Jesus Christ.
So then, my brothers and sisters, stand firm and hold on to the traditions we taught you, whether through the spoken word or through our letters.
May our Lord Jesus Christ himself and God our Father, who loved us and gave us everlasting comfort and good hope through grace,
comfort your hearts and strengthen you in every good deed and word.
Now, brothers and sisters, pray for us, so that the word of the Lord may spread and be honored, just as it was among you,
and so that we may be rescued from troublesome and wicked people, for not everyone has faith.
But the Lord is faithful. He will strengthen you and guard you from the evil one.
We have confidence in the Lord about you, that you have done what we command you, are doing it, and will continue to do it.
May the Lord direct your hearts toward the love of God and the endurance of Christ.
We command you, brothers and sisters, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, to keep away from every brother who lives in a disorderly way and not according to the teaching you received from us.
For you yourselves know how you ought to imitate us, because we did not behave in a disorderly way among you.
Nor did we eat anyone’s bread without paying for it. Instead, with toil and hardship we worked night and day so that we would not be a burden to any of you.
This was not because we lacked that right, but so that we could offer ourselves to you as an example for you to imitate.
For even when we were with you, we gave you this command: If someone is unwilling to work, do not let him eat either.
For we hear that some people among you live in a disorderly way, doing no work but meddling in other people’s affairs.
We command and urge such people in the Lord Jesus Christ to work quietly and eat their own bread.
But you, brothers and sisters, do not grow weary of doing good.
If anyone does not obey our word in this letter, take note of that person and do not associate with him, so that he may be ashamed.
Do not regard him as an enemy, but instruct him as a brother.
May the Lord of peace himself give you peace at all times and in every way. May the Lord be with you all.
This greeting I, Paul, have written with my own hand. This is the identifying mark in every letter; this is how I write.
May the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all.
